scope: Exact six-file R5 install/state02 first-failure collector only; fixed path/held FD closure, original failure/absence, qualification and necessary schema compatibility.

reviewed.read_scope: worker result initialization plus coordinator result initialization, success pin and failed_worker_result finally only

finding: No concrete new blocker found in this limited collection-only scope.
confirmed: Only six compiled fixed paths; callers provide two 64-hex external hashes, never arbitrary paths.
Path traversal opens each directory with NOFOLLOW, retains current dir FD, and closes file/current directory in finally on success, optional ENOENT or error.
Files must be root-owned single-link regular bounded receipts; before/after identity, timestamps and size, per-file/aggregate/output limits are checked.
Coordinator/stage externally pinned content and fixed source/package/nonce/no-UI scope are verified before output.
An existing worker result must match the coordinator complete path/bytes/SHA pin and exact worker package/state nonce/no-UI schema.

Actual matching worker source initializes the required result fields before result publication. The coordinator only sets failed_worker_result when a worker result actually exists; it is not initialized to None.
Four fixed worker artifacts may be absent. No state/installation success predicate is imposed, original text/bytes/SHA are preserved, and absence does not become qualification.
Every installation/runtime/Android/service/process/permission assertion in collector output remains false or zero; collector exit0 is collection only.
boundaries: The six reads are not an atomic filesystem snapshot. Missing means ENOENT at that member traversal/open, not perpetual absence.
Only held receipt bytes are checked; this is not a live named-path persistence, install, package retention, Main, UI or Android qualification.
No complete worker lifecycle review was performed. A failure to validate an existing unbound worker deliberately rejects collection rather than inventing a receipt.
